top_line: The Netherlands is mourning writer and comedian Paulien Cornelisse, who died of cancer at 50 while she was still on TV every night; in The Hague, MPs pushed back on a plan that would make hundreds of thousands of small savers pay tax on their savings.

stories.headline: Writer and comedian Paulien Cornelisse dies at 50
stories.summary: Paulien Cornelisse, a writer, comedian and columnist known for her playful books about language, died of cancer on Wednesday in Amsterdam's Antoni van Leeuwenhoek hospital. She was 50, and her loved ones were with her. She was diagnosed in 2024 and was still having chemotherapy this year. Cornelisse broke through with the 2009 bestseller 'Taal is zeg maar echt mijn ding' ('Language is, like, totally my thing'), which sold 700,000 copies. She was also on TV every night until her death, as the one-person jury on the quiz show De Slimste Mens, which she had presented with Herman van der Zandt since September 2025. Episodes were recorded before the summer, and she wore a hat or cap in each one because chemotherapy had made her hair fall out and she didn't want a wig. After talking with her family, the broadcaster KRO-NCRV dropped Wednesday's episode. The remaining episodes are being moved back by one day, and the broadcaster says it will announce the new dates. She had also been due back on stage with a new show, 'Waar was ik gebleven' ('Where was I'), which was to run exclusively at Amsterdam's DeLaMar theatre from late October. On Wednesday the theatre cancelled it and told ticket holders they would get refunds. Tributes came from Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who called her 'sharp, funny and incredibly kind'; from Amsterdam mayor Femke Halsema; from Volkskrant editor-in-chief Pieter Klok, who called her death 'a loss for the whole Netherlands'; and from Herman van der Zandt, who said she was 'sweet, funny and, even between treatments, wonderfully energetic.' Her last weekly column in de Volkskrant appeared just a week ago. In it she wondered about the word 'apegapen', a Dutch expression for being utterly exhausted.
stories.context: Cornelisse was something like a national language-watcher with a comedian's timing. Her bestsellers picked apart everyday Dutch: filler words, office jargon, the little things people say without meaning them. She also wrote a series of absurdist books about a guinea pig who works in an office. One of them won the NS Publieksprijs, a readers' book award run with the national railway, in 2025. That same year she wrote the Boekenweekessay, the essay commissioned every year for the national Book Week, about common Dutch words. It sold out on the second day of Book Week, which had never happened before. She had a lifelong love of Japan and made a documentary series about it called Tokidoki for the public broadcaster VPRO. De Slimste Mens ('The Smartest Person') is one of the most-watched quiz shows in the country, broadcast every weeknight. Being its jury is a famous TV role, which is why so many people saw her every evening right up to her death. She was born and raised in Amsterdam, went to the Barlaeus Gymnasium (a selective academic secondary school), studied psychology at the University of Amsterdam, and lived in Amsterdam with her partner Chris Bajema and their sons.
key_terms: Taal is zeg maar echt mijn ding (her 2009 bestseller: 'Language is, like, totally my thing')
De Slimste Mens ('The Smartest Person', nightly TV quiz)
cabaretier (comedian who performs one-person theatre shows; Dutch cabaret is closer to stand-up theatre than to song-and-dance)
De verwarde cavia ('The Confused Guinea Pig', her book series)
Boekenweekessay (the essay commissioned every year for the national Book Week)
apegapen (Dutch for being utterly exhausted; the subject of her last column)
Tokidoki (her Japan documentary series; Japanese for 'sometimes')
KRO-NCRV (the public broadcaster that makes De Slimste Mens)
open_questions: Will there be a public memorial or farewell for Paulien Cornelisse in Amsterdam?

findings.question: What are the remaining De Slimste Mens episodes with Cornelisse, and when will the cancelled episode be shown?
findings.answer: KRO-NCRV says it consulted her family and did not air the episode on Wednesday 30 September. The scheduled episodes, all already recorded, are being postponed by one day, and the new broadcast dates will be announced. That suggests the dropped episode moves to the next evening, but the broadcaster hasn't said how many episodes with her are left or given exact dates. She had presented the show with Herman van der Zandt since September 2025.

findings.question: What was the theatre show Het Parool says she planned to premiere in October, and will it go ahead in any form?
findings.answer: The show was 'Waar was ik gebleven' ('Where was I'), a new cabaret show directed by Gijsbert van der Wal. It was to run exclusively at DeLaMar in Amsterdam from late October 2026, with tickets on sale since May 2026, and was described as being about how life can't be controlled but your view of it can. On 30 September DeLaMar announced the show was cancelled and told ticket holders by email and text message about refunds. No future performances are planned. Listings disagree on the exact start date (26 or 27 October) and on whether the run ended in late December or mid-January.

findings.question: Will there be a public memorial or farewell for Paulien Cornelisse in Amsterdam?

stories.airtime_reason: Leads the show: rich life story, language humour, the hat-on-TV detail, cancelled show, last column on 'apegapen'

stories.headline: Border checks with Belgium and Germany end, but military police get wider powers to stop and check
stories.summary: The Royal Military Police (Koninklijke Marechaussee) are ending the temporary checks at the Belgian and German borders that were brought in by former asylum minister Marjolein Faber of the PVV. The checks began on 9 December 2024, were meant to last six months, and were extended several times. They ended on 30 September, as asylum and migration minister Bart van den Brink announced in May. The cabinet says it wants to keep fighting illegal migration and cross-border crime such as people smuggling, while responding to complaints from border towns, businesses and residents about the traffic disruption the checks caused. Between December 2024 and March 2026, about 600 foreign nationals were refused entry at the land borders, most because they had no valid travel documents or could not explain the purpose and length of their stay, and 270 people were arrested for offences including document fraud and people smuggling. The Marechaussee is not allowed to turn away asylum seekers at the border. As of 1 October, the Marechaussee returns to its regular system of spot checks in the border area, called Mobiel Toezicht Veiligheid (MTV), but with more room than before. Checks can take place anywhere within 20 kilometres of the Belgian and German borders, at changing times and places based on intelligence and risk. Officers can now check on the same road for up to 120 hours a month instead of 90, and the limit of six hours a day is gone. They still may only stop part of the passing traffic. On a selected train, every passenger can now be checked, and the same goes for a selected flight from another Schengen country. But no more than 25 percent of the trains or flights on a given route may be selected. The same number of staff who ran the temporary checks will be used for the new system. The Marechaussee welcomed the change, saying smugglers can no longer count on a checkpoint packing up after six hours. Germany is keeping its own temporary border checks until at least March 2027.
stories.context: The Marechaussee is a police force that is part of the military. It guards the borders, airports like Schiphol, and the royal family, a bit like a mix of US Customs and Border Protection and a military police service. Most of Europe belongs to the Schengen area, where there are normally no passport checks between member countries. Countries may bring back internal border checks only temporarily and must justify them. Faber's checks were a key promise of the previous cabinet, which was led by Geert Wilders' far-right PVV, and were meant to discourage asylum seekers from coming to the Netherlands. The Netherlands' national audit office, the Algemene Rekenkamer, found last year that the checks did not reduce migration, but could help fight illegal migration. The current cabinet is led by Prime Minister Rob Jetten of the centrist D66.
key_terms: Koninklijke Marechaussee / KMar (Royal Military Police, the border police)
Mobiel Toezicht Veiligheid / MTV (Mobile Security Monitoring: spot checks in the border zone)
Marjolein Faber (former PVV minister of asylum and migration)
Algemene Rekenkamer (Netherlands Court of Audit, the national audit office)

findings.question: Why did the Jetten cabinet decide not to extend Faber's border checks again: EU legal pressure, cost, or a policy choice?
findings.answer: The government presents it as a policy choice. Asylum and migration minister Bart van den Brink announced on 8 May 2026 that the checks would end on 30 September, and confirmed it on 24 September. The government says the expanded MTV system lets the Marechaussee keep targeting illegal migration and cross-border crime (including people smuggling) more flexibly, based on intelligence and risk. It also wants to respond to concerns from border towns, businesses and residents about disruption from the checks. The announcements I read say nothing about EU or Schengen legal pressure or about cost. One report says the same staff who ran the temporary checks will be used for the new system.

findings.question: How far from the border can the Marechaussee carry out the expanded MTV checks: still up to 20 km, or further?
findings.answer: Still up to 20 kilometres from the Belgian and German borders. The zone itself has not been widened. Within it, checks happen at changing places and times based on risk, and can cover cars, trucks, buses, trains, planes and boats. The government says this is a wider area than the temporary checks, which were mostly at the border crossings themselves.

findings.question: How many of the 600 people refused entry at the border were asylum seekers, and what happened to them?
findings.answer: I couldn't find a breakdown. But the Marechaussee is not allowed to refuse asylum seekers at the border: people who apply for asylum are let in and go into the asylum procedure. So the people refused were in principle not asylum applicants. According to NOS, people were turned away mainly because they had no valid travel documents or could not explain why and how long they wanted to stay. Separately, 270 people were arrested between December 2024 and March 2026 for crimes such as document fraud and people smuggling.

stories.airtime_reason: Needs Schengen and Marechaussee background; real twist that checks end but powers widen

stories.headline: Parliament balks at taxing small savers as budget debate opens
stories.previously: Finance Minister Heinen confirmed that the social security cuts are off the table. To help pay for a box 3 system that taxes shares only when they are sold, the cabinet proposed cutting the tax-free return from €1,800 to €1,000, which would pull roughly 850,000 more people into the tax. The cabinet also said a backstop cut to education could come into play if talks with the unions save too little.
stories.summary: On the first day of the annual budget debate in the House of Representatives, the plan to cut the tax-free return in box 3 to €1,000 found little support. JA21, ChristenUnie and the SGP oppose it, and Pro is against it on principle, so a majority looks out of reach. SGP MP Flach called it 'a fine on thrift or successful entrepreneurship'. JA21's Hoogeveen said it was disastrous for efforts to get more Dutch people investing their savings. After a barrage of questions, the coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA said they were willing to look at alternatives, and CDA MP Van Dijk called the plan 'an unfortunate point'. D66 MP Oosterhuis told Flach and ChristenUnie's Grinwis he would look at serious alternatives, but only ones that raise the same money from wealth taxation. The cut to the tax-free return is meant to bring in €473 million. Pro suggested taxing larger fortunes instead. No concrete alternative has been put forward yet. Many parties did welcome the switch to taxing gains only when assets are sold: from 2028 for shares, bonds and second homes, and from 2030 for crypto. The opposition was more critical of the income tax increase planned for next year. Both income tax bands go up in 2027, the first by 0.48 percentage points and the second by 0.60, net. This is partly offset by a higher labour tax credit, worth at most €173. Median purchasing power is still expected to fall slightly. The Council of State had already said that, despite the cabinet's promise that work should pay, €5.8 billion of the €6 billion in extra taxes in 2027 falls on workers, while the burden on businesses and the wealthy falls slightly. BBB MP Vermeer called it 'taking €200, giving back €100 and expecting you to be happy'. JA21 and Pro say they will only support the cabinet if that increase is scaled back. The Social Affairs budget now appears to have a majority, since Pro will back it. The fallback cut to education also caused friction. Oosterhuis dismissed the table showing it as the work of an 'overzealous civil servant' with no political weight. But VVD MP Van Eijk confirmed that cutting education is the agreed fallback if the social security savings fall short, and said more money 'has not necessarily led to better education'. Finance Minister Heinen and State Secretary Eerenberg give the cabinet's response today, and the Tax Plan debate starts in mid-October. Even before the new system starts, the cabinet wants to raise more from savers in 2027. It proposes cutting the current tax-free allowance on assets from €59,357 to €30,846 per person, back to its 2020 level, and raising the assumed return on investments by 1.5 percentage points. These measures were announced on 29 September and are not yet law. They still need a majority in both houses before the end of the year.
stories.context: The Algemene Financiële Beschouwingen is parliament's general debate on the cabinet's budget and finances, held each autumn. The governing coalition of D66, VVD and CDA has no majority in either house, so it needs opposition votes for every budget. Because the House already passed the earlier box 3 law, which now sits in the Senate, any new version has to go back through the House as an amendment bill (a novelle) before the Senate can vote. A 2021 Supreme Court ruling forced this overhaul, and the stopgap system in place since then costs the treasury about €3 billion a year.
key_terms: Algemene Financiële Beschouwingen (annual general budget debate)
vermogenswinstbelasting (tax on gains when assets are sold)
vermogensaanwasbelasting (tax on gains every year, including on paper)
heffingsvrij vermogen (tax-free allowance on assets, the current system)
novelle (amendment bill sent back to the House)
Raad van State (Council of State, the government's top legal adviser)

findings.question: What alternatives to the €1,000 tax-free return did JA21 and the SGP say the cabinet promised to look at, and did Heinen offer any in Thursday's reply?
findings.answer: I found no reports of specific alternatives being promised. The SGP's Flach asked whether the lower tax-free amount could be paid for another way. D66's Oosterhuis replied that he would look at a proposal from Flach if it met the conditions, and he told ChristenUnie's Grinwis he would consider serious alternatives within the same wealth domain. The measure is meant to raise €473 million. Pro suggested taking the money from larger fortunes instead, and VVD and CDA said they want to spare small savers. Reports say no firm commitment was made. Heinen's reply comes on Thursday 1 October, and I found no published account of it yet.

findings.question: How much does the planned income tax increase for 2027 cost a typical worker, and what exactly is the Council of State's criticism that work pays less?
findings.answer: I found no euro figure per typical worker. In 2027 the first income tax band rises by 0.48 percentage points and the second by 0.60, net. This is partly offset by a labour tax credit increase of at most €173. Median purchasing power is projected to be slightly negative: the lowest income group gains 0.2% and the two highest groups lose 0.2%. The Council of State said the cabinet claims work must pay, but its extra spending is paid for by higher taxes on labour. Of the €6 billion in extra taxes in 2027, €5.8 billion falls on workers, while the burden on businesses and the wealthy falls slightly. The Council warned that taxing labour heavily is not sustainable in the long term, given the ageing population.

findings.question: Is the cut to the tax-free allowance to €30,846 in 2027 already law, or part of this year's Tax Plan?
findings.answer: It is not law. It is a new cabinet proposal, announced on 29 September 2026 as part of the box 3 package, and returns the allowance to its 2020 level. It comes with a 1.5 percentage point rise in the assumed return on investments for 2027. Reporting describes it as part of the extra measures for the Tax Plan 2027. TPO reports that the box 3 law is being amended through a novelle, which is meant to be handled alongside the Tax Plan. The cabinet has asked the Council of State for urgent advice. Both houses need to approve it before the end of 2026.

stories.airtime_reason: Follow-up but many new turns: coalition wobble, income tax hike, Council of State critique, education fallback, savings allowance cut

stories.headline: Mortgage rates hit a high for the year as the government moves to regulate estate agents
stories.summary: The average 10-year fixed mortgage rate with a National Mortgage Guarantee has risen to 4.5 percent, the highest this year, NU.nl reports. It stood at around 4.1 to 4.2 percent as recently as late August and mid-September. The rise is driven mainly by higher rates on the capital markets, where banks raise money for their loans, amid worries about inflation, energy prices and geopolitical tension. The European Central Bank has kept its deposit rate at 2.25 percent. Higher rates directly reduce how much buyers can borrow. For example, a couple earning 90,000 euros a year can borrow about 395,000 euros at 4.5 percent, compared with about 413,000 euros at 3.5 percent. Monthly payments rise faster still, by about 200 euros per percentage point on a 350,000-euro loan. Even so, house prices are not expected to fall for now. More homes are coming up for sale, but demand still far outstrips supply. Het Parool reports that Amsterdam's housing market keeps cooling, a trend ABN Amro researchers expect to spread across the country. In the second quarter, Amsterdam prices were only 0.8 percent higher than a year earlier, against 4.2 percent nationally and around 8 percent in Groningen. ABN Amro expects prices to stay flat or dip slightly for the rest of this year, and has cut its forecast for 2027 price growth to 2.5 percent. Separately, Housing Minister Boekholt-O'Sullivan of D66 says she will take oversight of estate agents away from the industry itself. All agents will have to sign up to a government register to work, and there will be a complaints desk and a disputes committee. In serious cases, the committee can strike an agent off the register, which would bar them from working in the Netherlands. Agents will also have to show buyers the bidding log, the record of every bid made on a home. The minister said she had hoped the industry would sort this out itself, but agents' associations told her they could not control rogue members. Research she commissioned found almost a third of respondents had had at least one bad experience with an agent, but only 2 percent filed an official complaint. She will work with PVV MP Mooiman, who has his own bill for a register, rules of conduct, outside oversight and fines. Concrete proposals are due in early 2027.
stories.context: In the Netherlands, homes are usually sold through bidding run by the seller's agent. Buyers bid blind and often well over the asking price, which is why people worry about agents nudging bids up. Unlike in most US states, there is currently no government licence to work as an estate agent. Nationale Hypotheekgarantie (NHG) is a government-backed mortgage guarantee for homes below a set price, roughly comparable to FHA backing, and it comes with a lower interest rate. Dutch lending rules tie how much you can borrow to the interest rate, so higher rates quickly shrink buyers' budgets.

findings.question: How far have Amsterdam house prices or sales slowed, according to Het Parool's report on the cooling market?
findings.answer: The Het Parool article could not be opened directly. A news aggregator lists the piece under AD, a paper with the same owner, and says it is based on ABN Amro research published 1 October 2026. ABN Amro expects the Amsterdam cooling to spread to the rest of the Netherlands. According to the Reformatorisch Dagblad's report on that research, Amsterdam prices rose only 0.8% year on year in Q2 2026. The national figure was 4.2% and Groningen's about 8%. ABN Amro raised its 2026 national price forecast to 3.8% (from 3%) and cut 2027 to 2.5% (from 4%). It expects prices to stay flat or dip slightly for the rest of 2026, and sales to fall 5.5% in 2027.

findings.question: Why are mortgage rates rising: higher capital market rates or ECB policy?
findings.answer: Mainly higher capital market rates, not ECB action. Banks fund mortgages partly on the capital markets and pass on their higher costs with a delay. The ECB has kept its deposit rate at 2.25%. Behind the rise in market rates are financial-market unrest, concerns about inflation and energy prices, and geopolitical tension that began with the US–Iran conflict in March 2026. ABN Amro now also expects two ECB rate hikes in 2027. The NHG 10-year rate was 4.10% on 24 August and about 4.16–4.17% around 10–11 September. Analyst Van Bruggen had named 4.5% as the most likely scenario.

findings.question: How much less can a typical buyer borrow at 4.5 percent compared with earlier this year?
findings.answer: No source gives a direct comparison with the start of 2026. An example from beginner.nl: a couple earning €90,000 a year with no debts can borrow €412,542 at 3.5%, €403,737 at 4% and €395,216 at 4.5%. That is about €17,000 less per percentage point. Monthly costs rise faster: about €200 a month per percentage point on a €350,000 loan.

stories.airtime_reason: Two connected strands relevant to a newcomer: rates and borrowing math, Amsterdam cooling, blind bidding and agent register

stories.headline: Prosecutors to seek jail for attacks on police, paramedics and other public workers, as rail staff sound the alarm
stories.summary: From Thursday, a new guideline from the Public Prosecution Service (Openbaar Ministerie) requires that every case of violence against people with a public role goes to court. These cases can no longer be settled with a prosecutor's fine or community service. Prosecutors must seek double the usual sentence, with prison as the starting point. The guideline covers police officers, emergency workers, security staff, referees, public transport staff, teachers, judges, lawyers, politicians, council staff and journalists. Justice Minister David van Weel gave an example: attempted serious assault on an emergency worker, without a weapon, by a first offender, and causing no injury. That would in principle bring a demand of three months in prison, against 80 hours of community service if the victim were an ordinary member of the public. These are starting points: prosecutors can still adjust for the circumstances of a case, and judges keep their discretion. The step follows pressure from MPs after New Year's Eve violence, when police and firefighters were attacked and sometimes lured into ambushes. Police faced almost 13,000 violent incidents in 2025. On the same day, the rail workers' union VVMC sent an urgent letter to politicians. NS figures show 5,088 reports of aggression against staff so far this year, including 1,368 involving physical violence and 105 threats with a weapon. That compares with 2,672 in all of 2023 and 6,442 in 2025. The union cites conductors knocked unconscious at Rotterdam Blaak and Den Dolder, and an arrest at Almere Centrum where an employee was badly bitten on the thumb. It wants more NS security staff on trains, and it wants back the enforcement powers that senior conductors lost in 2022. NS dropped those powers as a cost-saving measure, and since then conductors can no longer write official reports or check people's personal details in the population register. NS says it shares the concerns, is giving all conductors body cameras, is testing batons for its security staff and is hiring more. The union also points to rival operator Arriva, which told staff on the Vechtdal line between Zwolle and Emmen to let fare dodgers go without a fine when they turn threatening, instead of waiting around 25 minutes for police. Staff did so at least 16 times in the first two weeks. Arriva says the new access to the driving licence register will not solve the problem on that line.
stories.context: The Openbaar Ministerie is the national prosecution service. Unlike US district attorneys, prosecutors are not elected, and national guidelines largely set what sentences they ask for. Since 2006, the law has allowed sentences 200 percent heavier for attacks on people in public roles. But research by the justice ministry's research centre WODC found prosecutors rarely used it. MPs have also proposed banning community service outright for these attacks. The Council of State and judges criticised that idea because it would take away judges' discretion. NS is the national railway. Its 'Veiligheid & Service' staff are security officers with limited police powers. Separately, the cabinet announced this week that public transport security officers can now get access to the driving licence register, so they can identify people who carry no ID.
key_terms: College van procureurs-generaal (Board of Procurators General, the prosecution service's national leadership)

findings.question: Does the new guideline require an unconditional prison sentence (as DutchNews reports) or make prison the starting point with double the usual sentence (as NOS reports)? How do the two descriptions fit together?
findings.answer: Both outlets describe the same guideline, with different emphasis. NOS says every case must go to court, prosecutors must seek double the normal sentence, and prison is the starting point instead of community service. DutchNews says prosecutors will demand prison instead of fines or community service, but also says these demands 'remain a starting point from which prosecutors and judges can still exercise discretion according to the circumstances of a case.' So prison is what prosecutors ask for by default, not a mandatory unconditional sentence, and judges decide the outcome. Both give the same example: in principle, three months in prison instead of 80 hours of community service.

findings.question: Why did senior NS conductors lose their enforcement powers in 2022, and is the cabinet considering giving them back?
findings.answer: NS management dropped the special enforcement officer (boa) status for senior conductors to save money, about €5.7 million a year, as part of cost-cutting after heavy coronavirus-era losses. NS estimated the powers were used in only 2–4% of incidents. The works council objected, but in 2022 the Amsterdam Enterprise Chamber ruled that NS could go ahead (ECLI:NL:GHAMS:2022:1997). Since then, conductors cannot write official reports (processen-verbaal) themselves or check the population register (BRP). VVMC wants the powers restored. No source found shows the cabinet is considering restoring them; its only step so far is giving public transport security officers access to the driving licence register.

findings.question: How has the Arriva decision to stop fining aggressive fare dodgers on the Vechtdal line between Zwolle and Emmen played out?
findings.answer: An internal Arriva memo from late August told conductors and security officers on the Zwolle–Emmen line to let fare dodgers go when aggression threatens, rather than wait an average of about 25 minutes for police. Passengers who show ID can still be fined. Arriva says staff let passengers go at least 16 times in the first two weeks. It links much of the trouble to asylum seekers from the Ter Apel reception centre, and says serious incidents rose from 29 in 2024 to 51 in 2025. Reactions: the VVD in Zwolle asked questions about local safety. VVMC said the answer should be more checks and more security staff, not letting people go. Arriva, ProRail, police and the province have discussed screening passengers at stations before they board, and Emmen has brought back such checks. According to De Stentor (29 September), Arriva says the new driving licence register access will not help on this line and that it must wait until 2028. The reason for the 2028 date could not be confirmed.

stories.airtime_reason: New sentencing guideline plus vivid rail-staff figures, lost conductor powers and Arriva's let-them-go policy

stories.headline: Health inspectorate halts Amsterdam trial of crack-addiction medicine
stories.summary: Amsterdam's trial of treating crack users with dexamphetamine, a drug normally prescribed for ADHD, has been put on hold. The Health and Youth Care Inspectorate (IGJ) stopped production of the medicine at a hospital it will not name, citing an ongoing inspection procedure. An IGJ spokesperson told DutchNews the inspectorate is 'concerned about the quality of the medicine', and said the investigation began before the trial did. The inspectorate has not said what the quality concerns are. The city says the first participants had already received the drug, and their treatment has been interrupted. Alderman Alexander Scholtes said he could not say how many people are affected. The research team has until the end of the year to decide whether the study can go on. The city called the halt 'unexpected and for reasons that are unclear to us'. Scholtes said it means 'the only promising method' for treating heavily addicted people is now off the table. He and Mayor Femke Halsema wrote to Health Minister Sophie Hermans, asking her to review the decision and bring all parties together before 1 November. They also want a short-term protocol that would let doctors prescribe the short-acting form of dexamphetamine, or the related drug lisdexamfetamine, to people addicted to cocaine. Hermans has since responded but did not commit to the meeting. She said she understands the city's concerns but stressed that the inspectorate's oversight is independent: 'I have confidence in their judgment.' The long-acting form of the drug was developed over 12 years by the REDUCE project, whose partners include the city health service GGD Amsterdam. Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht back the study. GGD Amsterdam estimates there are 3,000 to 9,000 crack users in the city, many of them homeless or with mental health problems.
stories.context: Crack use is rising in the Netherlands, and a 2023 report by the Trimbos Institute and the support service Mainline estimated around 27,900 problematic users nationwide. The idea behind the trial is similar to methadone for heroin users: give a controlled stimulant to reduce cravings. The IGJ is the national health inspectorate, an independent watchdog roughly comparable in role to parts of the FDA and state health inspectors. A wethouder is a city alderman, a member of the mayor's executive team who runs a policy area. Amsterdam has a long tradition of pragmatic, harm-reduction drug policy.
key_terms: Inspectie Gezondheidszorg en Jeugd / IGJ (Health and Youth Care Inspectorate)
REDUCE (the research project behind the medicine)
open_questions: Which hospital was making the dexamphetamine for the REDUCE trial, and what quality problems did the IGJ find?

findings.question: Which hospital was making the dexamphetamine for the REDUCE trial, and what quality problems did the IGJ find?
How many participants were already receiving the medicine, and what happens to their treatment now?
findings.answer: No number has been published. Alderman Scholtes said he could not say how many people were affected. NH Nieuws reports that participants who had already started on dexamphetamine have had their treatment interrupted. Binnenlands Bestuur reports that the research team has to decide by the end of the year whether the study will continue. Amsterdam is also asking for a short-term protocol that would allow doctors to prescribe short-acting dexamphetamine or lisdexamfetamine to people addicted to cocaine.

findings.question: Has Health Minister Sophie Hermans responded to Halsema and Scholtes' request for a meeting?
findings.answer: Yes. According to Binnenlands Bestuur (30 September 2026), Hermans said she understood Amsterdam's concerns but stressed that the IGJ's oversight is independent: 'Ik heb vertrouwen in hun oordeel' ('I have confidence in their judgment'). She noted that the IGJ will not comment while its procedure is ongoing. The reported response does not include any commitment to bring the parties together before 1 November.

stories.airtime_reason: Local harm-reduction story with a clear tension, but key facts (which hospital, what problem) are missing

stories.headline: Netherlands struggles to send asylum seekers back to Italy, threatens to pull funding
stories.summary: The Netherlands is still struggling to send asylum seekers back to Italy, even though the two countries agreed in June that transfers would resume. Asylum and Migration Minister Bart van den Brink (CDA) told parliament on Wednesday that the Netherlands will not pay its solidarity contribution to Italy if Italy keeps refusing to take people back. "If something doesn't work, we won't pay," he said. He plans to raise the issue with other EU ministers and the European Commission. The contribution is part of the new EU Migration Pact, which took effect on 12 June. Under the pact, countries such as the Netherlands help Mediterranean states like Italy, Greece and Spain, either by taking in asylum seekers or by paying. The Netherlands chose to pay. Its share of the EU's €420 million solidarity pool for 2026 is about €11 million. On 3 June, Van den Brink and Italian interior minister Matteo Piantedosi signed a declaration of intent in Rome. Italy would again accept asylum seekers who travelled through Italy to the Netherlands and applied there on or after 12 June. In practice, little has happened. A European Commission report found that in the first three weeks of the pact, Italy carried out none of the twelve transfer requests it received from EU member states. Dutch courts have also repeatedly blocked transfers, including a 22 September ruling in three cases. The judges said Van den Brink had not shown that Italy has reserved reception places for returned asylum seekers.
stories.context: Under the EU's Dublin rules, the country where an asylum seeker first enters the EU is usually responsible for their application. Other countries can transfer people back there. Italy, where many migrants arrive across the Mediterranean, has for years largely refused to take back such 'Dublin claimants', which frustrates northern European countries like the Netherlands. Sending people back is a major theme in Dutch migration politics.
key_terms: Dublinclaimanten (asylum seekers who must be sent back to the EU country they entered first)
overdracht (transfer of an asylum seeker to another EU country)

findings.question: What financial support is the Netherlands giving Italy, how much is it, and what is it meant for?
findings.answer: The money is the Netherlands' 'solidarity contribution' under the EU Migration and Asylum Pact, which took effect on 12 June 2026. Under the pact, member states either take in asylum seekers from countries under pressure, such as Italy, Greece and Spain, or pay instead. The Netherlands chose to pay. According to the 2027 Asylum and Migration budget, the EU solidarity pool for 2026 is 21,000 relocations or €420 million. The Dutch share is 5.2%, which comes to €10.95 million. The money is meant to ease the burden on the frontline Mediterranean states. No source said how much of it goes to Italy specifically.

findings.question: What exactly did Italy promise the Netherlands, and when?
findings.answer: On 3 June 2026, Minister Van den Brink and Italian interior minister Piantedosi signed a declaration of intent in Rome. From 12 June, when the Migration Pact took effect, Italy would again take back asylum seekers who had travelled through Italy to the Netherlands. People who registered in the Netherlands before 12 June would not be sent back (a 'clean slate'). The two countries also agreed to work more closely on returning rejected asylum seekers and on fighting people smuggling in Algeria, Tunisia and Libya. Van den Brink later told the courts that Piantedosi had assured him new reception places would be created for transferred asylum seekers. In its 4 September ruling, the Hague district court called the declaration's commitments vague.

findings.question: How many asylum seekers is the Netherlands trying to transfer to Italy, and how many have actually been sent back this year?
findings.answer: No source gave the total number of Dutch transfer cases involving Italy or the number actually sent back this year. A 4 September 2026 court ruling cites a European Commission report from July. It found that in the first three weeks of the pact, Italy carried out none of the twelve transfer requests it received from EU member states. The ruling also mentions one transfer on 19 August 2026, which the court said did not show that Italy was cooperating consistently. Dutch courts have since blocked several more transfers, including three cases decided on 22 September.

findings.question: Which Dutch minister is in charge of this, and what deadline has been set for Italy?
findings.answer: The minister in charge is Bart van den Brink (CDA), Minister of Asylum and Migration. He made the funding threat during a parliamentary debate on 30 September 2026, saying 'if something doesn't work, we won't pay', and said he would raise the issue with EU counterparts and the European Commission. No reports mentioned a specific deadline for Italy.

stories.airtime_reason: Dublin rules need a line of context; otherwise one threat plus court setbacks

stories.headline: Van Gogh painting of chestnut trees in bloom expected to fetch a record $180 million
stories.summary: Sotheby's expects a record price when it auctions 'Châtaigniers en fleurs' ('Chestnut Trees in Blossom') by Vincent van Gogh in New York on 18 November. It values the painting at about $180 million, or €158 million. Sotheby's says the final price could be $200 million or more. That would comfortably beat the current Van Gogh auction record of $117 million, paid for 'Orchard with Cypresses' at Christie's in 2022. Van Gogh painted the flowering chestnut tree in May 1890, days after he arrived in Auvers-sur-Oise outside Paris. He died there two months later. The painting is being sold by the children of Argentine collectors Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier and sugar magnate Carlos Pedro Blaquier. The couple bought it in 1975, and it has stayed in the family's private collection in South America ever since. It was last shown in public at the Guggenheim in New York in 1964. The work leads a sale of twelve works from the Blaquier-Arrieta collection, including a Cézanne portrait, which Sotheby's expects to bring in around $450 million in total.
stories.context: Van Gogh is a source of national pride for the Dutch. His museum in Amsterdam is one of the most visited in the country, and his paintings rarely come up for sale. A price this high would put the painting among the most expensive ever sold at auction, and the Dutch watch these sales closely.
key_terms: Châtaigniers en fleurs ('Chestnut Trees in Blossom')

findings.question: When and where will Sotheby's auction 'Châtaigniers en fleurs'?
findings.answer: At Sotheby's in New York on 18 November 2026. It leads a sale of 12 works from the Blaquier-Arrieta collection, which together are expected to fetch around $450 million. Sotheby's has guaranteed the collection but would not say for how much.

findings.question: Who is selling the painting, and where has it been for the past sixty years?
findings.answer: The sellers are the children of Argentine collectors Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier and her husband, sugar magnate Carlos Pedro Blaquier. The couple bought the painting from Wildenstein in 1975, and it has been in their private collection in South America since then. It was last shown in public in 1964 at the Guggenheim in New York, which fits the 'sixty years' figure. Wire reports round this to 'half a century'. Before the Blaquiers, it belonged to Theo van Gogh, then his widow and son, and later to publisher Samuel Fischer and Capitol Records co-founder George 'Buddy' DeSylva.

findings.question: When and where did Van Gogh paint it, and what is the current auction record for a Van Gogh?
findings.answer: Van Gogh painted it in May 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, outside Paris, days after he arrived there following his release from the asylum. He died two months later. The current Van Gogh auction record is $117 million, paid for 'Orchard with Cypresses' (1888) at Christie's New York in November 2022, in the sale of Paul Allen's collection. Sotheby's says the chestnut painting could reach $200 million or more.

stories.airtime_reason: Fun record-price hook with a nice back-story, but little Dutch angle

stories.headline: Study: TikTok queues at Fabel Friet knock thousands off neighbours' home values
stories.previously: About twenty residents of the Nine Streets, backed by around 80 others, went to court against the city's renewal of Fabel Friet's permit over daily TikTok queues, litter and crowds. The city says the shop's crowd managers and other measures keep the nuisance acceptable.
stories.summary: Homes near Fabel Friet, the TikTok-famous chip shop on Runstraat, sell for less than similar homes a few streets away, according to research by TU Delft PhD candidate Rosa van der Drift, published in the academic journal Regional Studies. She looked at the sale prices of 6,233 Amsterdam homes between 2015 and 2023 and compared homes near the shop with similar ones further away, taking into account things like size and condition. Homes within 500 meters of the shop sold for 4.88 percent less on average, about €41,000. Within 70 meters, the gap rose to 11.4 percent. Fabel Friet opened on Runstraat in 2020, and the long queues started after it went viral on TikTok in 2022, so only the last couple of years of the study period fall in the TikTok era. The study does not pin down the cause, but possible reasons include crowds, noise, the queue itself and litter. The judge in the residents' case against the city is expected to rule in a few weeks. Meanwhile, an opinion piece in Het Parool told the complainers they are 'warmly welcome in Purmerend', a town north of Amsterdam.
stories.context: Fabel Friet has become a test case in Amsterdam's long fight over overtourism in the historic centre, where residents feel their neighbourhoods are being turned into attractions. A drop of €41,000 is a striking figure in a city with some of the highest house prices in the country. The Purmerend jab reflects a familiar retort to canal-belt residents: if you live in the centre, you have to accept the crowds.
key_terms: Runstraat (its street in the Nine Streets)
friet / patat (Dutch fries; the word you use depends on the region)

findings.question: When did Fabel Friet open and go viral on TikTok? Does a study covering 2015–2023 cover the TikTok years, or mostly earlier?
findings.answer: The founders started with a fries bike in 2019 and opened the small (about 18 m²) shop on Runstraat in 2020, during the pandemic. It went viral on TikTok and the queues began in 2022. That means most of the 2015–2023 study period comes before the shop existed or went viral, and only about 2022–2023 falls in the TikTok-queue era. AT5 says the reporting does not mention any split between before and after the shop went viral, and no outlet explains how the study handled the timing.

findings.question: Is Rosa van der Drift's TU Delft study a published paper or a student thesis, and did it control for other local factors?
findings.answer: It is not a student thesis. Van der Drift is a PhD candidate at TU Delft, and NL Times reports the research was published in the academic journal Regional Studies. AT5 says the study compared the 6,233 sales with similar homes further away, taking into account the size and condition of the property. The exact figure was 4.88 percent within 500 m. The study does not establish what causes the lower prices. None of the articles reviewed give full details on any other controls, such as other local amenities or tourist hotspots.

stories.airtime_reason: Follow-up; the €41,000 finding and timing caveat are fun to discuss, plus the Purmerend jab

events.name: Joe Hisaishi Film Music with the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra
events.when: Friday 2 to Sunday 4 October, various times
events.blurb: Composer Joe Hisaishi conducts the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra and plays piano himself. The programme includes his Studio Ghibli scores for Spirited Away, Ponyo and Howl's Moving Castle, shown with film clips on a big screen. It's the orchestra's first visit to the city's biggest concert hall.
events.note: The orchestra's run at the Ziggo Dome also includes a Beethoven's Ninth night, so check the date before booking
events.source: I amsterdam calendar [23761fb6]; I amsterdam weekend guide

events.name: Chez Matisse (opening weekend)
events.blurb: A major new exhibition with more than 80 works by Henri Matisse, including his famous La Blouse roumaine. It shows how his bold colours and shapes changed modern art and influenced artists like Picasso, Rothko and Newman.
events.note: Opening weekend; the exhibition runs until 14 February
events.source: I amsterdam calendar [20f9816f]; I amsterdam weekend guide

events.name: Afrovibes Festival
events.when: Thursday 1 October from 19:15; Friday 2 and Saturday 3 October from 19:30 (De Brakke Grond). Also 3–4 October at Bijlmer Parktheater and Framer Framed
events.where: Vlaams Cultuurhuis de Brakke Grond, city centre (plus Bijlmer Parktheater and Framer Framed)
events.blurb: The 23rd edition of this festival of dance, theatre, music, spoken word and performance by artists from Africa and the African diaspora. This year's theme is land, ancestry and belonging.
events.note: The Bijlmer Parktheater dates may still change
events.source: I amsterdam calendar [1f364eb2]; I amsterdam weekend guide

events.name: IJver's anniversary party with free oysters and bitterballen
events.where: IJver Amsterdam, Scheepsbouwkade 72, NDSM Wharf, Amsterdam-Noord
events.blurb: IJver is celebrating 7.5 years, and the NDSM Wharf turns 132. The party has 1,000 free oysters, 1,000 free bitterballen (Dutch deep-fried snacks), €2.50 draught beer and spritz, and a live DJ. It's a good excuse to explore the old shipyard area.
events.note: No sign-up needed; free food lasts while supplies last
events.source: I amsterdam weekend guide; Your Little Black Book

events.name: Sunday Market at Westergas
events.blurb: A relaxed Sunday market with street food, local makers, gifts and art. You can combine it with a walk through the park.
events.source: I amsterdam weekend guide; Your Little Black Book
